To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the power output in MFCs is predicted by the fraction of species that are anaerobic respiring bacteria with low potential electron acceptors, and that the power output is independent of the species that are present in the community.

MFCs with fermentable feedstock and natural inoculum develop a complex community of fermenters, methanogens, acetogens and anode respirers, and that the power yield is predicted by the metabolic composition of the anode community, specifically by the fraction of anode-respiring species.
MFCs inoculated with a natural community and fed with fermentable substrates are a two stage system, with fermentation followed by anaerobic anode respiration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of MFCs for the treatment of organic wastes, and the production of bioelectricity from organic waste streams.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the metabolic composition of the anode biofilm is an important predictor for the electric yield in MFCs.
MFCs with fermentative feedstocks can be started with a wide range of natural inocula and will develop into a community of fermenters and anaerobic respirers.
power output of an MFC is a complex function of the composition of the community in terms of metabolic capability, but that the presence of low potential respirators is the most important factor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the power output of an MFC with fermentable feedstock and natural inoculum depends on the fraction of the community that is able to use terminal electron acceptor with a low red-ox potential.
the metabolic composition of the anode community predicts the electrical power in MFCs.
